review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

21:1.sourceText: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν πλουσίους.
21:1.targetText: Then Jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,

groups.note: The article with the participle, τοὺς βάλλοντας ("those putting"), is rendered the … putting, with πλουσίους ("rich") as the head noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle Ἀναβλέψας and the verb εἶδεν.
English coordinator; the participle Ἀναβλέψας is rendered as the finite verb looked up.

21:2.sourceText: εἶδεν δέ τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ λεπτὰ δύο,
21:2.targetText: and He saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.

groups.note: ἐκεῖ, "there" (into the treasury), is rendered by in.

21:3.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
21:3.targetText: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
ὅτι introduces the statement and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English spells out whom πάντων ("all") compares her with.

21:4.sourceText: πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
21:4.targetText: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”

groups.note: οὗτοι, "these", is rendered they.
τοῦ περισσεύοντος, "what is left over", is rendered surplus.
ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, "put into the offerings", is rendered contributed.
τοῦ ὑστερήματος, "the lack", is rendered poverty.
τὸν βίον, "the livelihood", is rendered to live on.
The relative ὃν ("which") is not a separate English word in all she had.

21:5.sourceText: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται, εἶπεν
21:5.targetText: As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,

groups.note: The genitive-absolute participle λεγόντων is rendered as an As-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB makes the temple the subject of the how-clause, so περί ("about") is not expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English specifies who τινων ("some") were.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb εἶπεν.

21:6.sourceText: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
21:6.targetText: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

groups.note: The hanging phrase Ταῦτα ἅ, "these things that", is rendered As for what.
ἡμέραι, "days", is rendered the time.
ἐν αἷς, "in which", is rendered when.
ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται, "which will not be thrown down", is turned into the positive every one will be thrown down.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds here, pointing to what they were looking at.

21:7.sourceText: ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
21:7.targetText: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”

groups.note: ὅταν, "when", introduces what the sign points to and is rendered that.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτόν ("him") unexpressed.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the quotation marks.
The connective οὖν is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the question τί τὸ σημεῖον has none.

21:8.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες Ἐγώ εἰμι, καί Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
21:8.targetText: Jesus answered, “See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names Jesus.
μή after Βλέπετε, "lest", is rendered that … not.
πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω, "go after", is rendered follow.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a predicate; Ἐγώ εἰμι ("I am") has none.

21:9.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
21:9.targetText: When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.”

groups.note: εὐθέως, "immediately", is rendered imminent.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The connective γάρ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος has none.

21:10.sourceText: Τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,
21:10.targetText: Then He told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.

21:11.sourceText: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λοιμοὶ καὶ λιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἔσται.
21:11.targetText: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.

groups.note: κατὰ τόπους, "place by place", is one distributive phrase.
BSB's English order, famines before pestilences, follows a reading that differs from N1904 here.
Each clause has its own verb (ἔσονται … ἔσται); English states There will be once for both.
τε, "and", joining this second clause to the list, is rendered along with.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle τε is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The καί is replaced by a list comma in this English wording.

21:12.sourceText: πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
21:12.targetText: But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.

groups.note: ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ … τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν, "they will lay their hands on", is the idiom seize.
The participle παραδιδόντες, "delivering", is rendered as a finite verb.
The passive participle ἀπαγομένους, "(you) being led away", is rendered actively they will bring you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; διώξουσιν has none expressed.
English supplies the object; παραδιδόντες has none expressed.
English coordinator; the participle ἀπαγομένους is rendered as a finite verb.

21:13.targetText: This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.

groups.note: ἀποβήσεται, "it will turn out (for you)", is rendered This will be … opportunity.

21:14.sourceText: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι·
21:14.targetText: So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.

groups.note: θέτε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις, "put in your hearts", is the idiom make up your mind.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies how; the Greek has only the infinitive ἀπολογηθῆναι ("to make a defense").

21:15.sourceText: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν, ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
21:15.targetText: For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.

groups.note: στόμα, "mouth", is rendered speech.
οὐ … ἅπαντες, "all … not", is rendered none of.
The article with the participle, οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ("those opposing"), is rendered adversaries.
ὑμῖν, "(opposing) you", is rendered your.

21:16.sourceText: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,
21:16.targetText: You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death.

groups.note: The active θανατώσουσιν, "they will put to death", is rendered as a passive.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

21:17.sourceText: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
21:17.targetText: And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:18.sourceText: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται·
21:18.targetText: Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.

groups.note: The καί here is contrastive and is rendered Yet.
οὐ μή is the emphatic double negative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:19.sourceText: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσεσθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
21:19.targetText: By your patient endurance you will gain your souls.

groups.note: BSB's Greek differs at this word; the English future renders N1904's κτήσεσθε ("you will gain").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:20.sourceText: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἱερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
21:20.targetText: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.

groups.note: The imperative γνῶτε, "know", is rendered you will know.

unmappedSource.reason: τότε ("then") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:21.sourceText: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,
21:21.targetText: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.

groups.note: The article οἱ with ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ means those in Judea.
ἐν μέσῳ, "in the midst of", is rendered in.
αὐτῆς, "her", refers to Jerusalem and is rendered the city.
μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς, "let them not enter", is rendered let … stay out of.
αὐτήν, "her", refers to Jerusalem and is rendered the city.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is replaced by a comma in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause for the article phrase οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ.

21:22.sourceText: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
21:22.targetText: For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.

groups.note: τοῦ πλησθῆναι, "so that … may be fulfilled", is rendered actively to fulfill.
The article with the participle, τὰ γεγραμμένα ("the things written"), is rendered that is written.

21:23.sourceText: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,
21:23.targetText: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.

groups.note: οὐαί, "woe", is rendered as the exclamation How miserable.
ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις, "for those having [a child] in the womb", is the idiom for pregnant.
The dative τῷ λαῷ, "for the people", is rendered against … people.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ("in those days") the subject, so ἐν is not expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the exclamation οὐαί has none.

21:24.sourceText: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
21:24.targetText: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

groups.note: The dative στόματι, "by the mouth", is the idiom for the edge of a sword.
ἄχρι οὗ is one conjunction, until.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

21:25.sourceText: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,
21:25.targetText: There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.

groups.note: ἐν ἀπορίᾳ, "in perplexity", is rendered bewildered.
The genitive ἤχους, "at the roaring", gives the cause of the perplexity.
σάλος is the rolling surge of the sea, rendered the surging of the waves.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

21:26.sourceText: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ· αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
21:26.targetText: Men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

groups.note: The article with the participle, τῶν ἐπερχομένων ("of the things coming upon"), is rendered over what is coming upon.

21:27.sourceText: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
21:27.targetText: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:28.sourceText: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
21:28.targetText: When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”

groups.note: The genitive-absolute participle ἀρχομένων is rendered as a When-clause.
ἀνακύψατε, "straighten up", is rendered stand up.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:29.sourceText: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
21:29.targetText: Then Jesus told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb εἶπεν.

21:30.sourceText: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
21:30.targetText: When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.

groups.note: προβάλωσιν, "they put forth", is used of trees putting out leaves.
The participle βλέποντες, "seeing", is rendered you can see.

unmappedSource.reason: ἤδη ("already", twice) is not expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle βλέποντες is rendered as a finite verb.

21:31.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.
21:31.targetText: So also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.

groups.note: The emphatic ὑμεῖς, "you also", appears as the you of the when-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:32.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
21:32.targetText: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

groups.note: οὐ μή is the emphatic double negative.
ἕως ἄν is one conjunction, until.
The neuter plural πάντα means all things.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the saying is not expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:33.sourceText: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
21:33.targetText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

groups.note: οὐ μή is the emphatic double negative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

21:34.sourceText: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μή ποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη
21:34.targetText: But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life—and that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.

groups.note: μή ποτε, "lest", is rendered or.
N1904 prints ὡς παγίς ("like a snare") at the start of 21:35; BSB ends 21:34 with it.

21:35.sourceText: ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
21:35.targetText: For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.

groups.note: The article with the participle, τοὺς καθημένους ("those sitting"), is rendered who dwell.

sourceMoved.reason: N1904 prints ὡς παγίς ("like a snare") here; BSB renders it at the end of 21:34.

21:36.sourceText: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
21:36.targetText: So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”

groups.note: The article with the participle, τὰ μέλλοντα ("the things about to"), is rendered that is about.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ταῦτα ("these things") unexpressed; all renders πάντα alone.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle δεόμενοι is rendered as a second imperative.

21:37.sourceText: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν.
21:37.targetText: Every day Jesus taught at the temple, but every evening He went out to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.

groups.note: The periphrastic Ἦν … διδάσκων, "He was teaching", is rendered taught.
τὰς ἡμέρας, "during the days", is rendered Every day.
τὰς … νύκτας, "during the nights", is rendered every evening.
The participle ἐξερχόμενος, "going out", is rendered as the finite verb He went out.
The finite ηὐλίζετο, "He lodged for the night", is rendered as the purpose phrase to spend the night.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves τὸ καλούμενον ("called") unexpressed and gives Mount of Olives as a plain name.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb Ἦν … διδάσκων.

21:38.sourceText: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
21:38.targetText: And early in the morning all the people would come to hear Him at the temple.

groups.note: ὤρθριζεν, "came early in the morning", is rendered early in the morning … would come.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") unexpressed; Him is the object of hear.
